scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

First, I need to evaluate if selling the games was morally acceptable. The key points here are the roommate's inaction. He left everything, didn't respond to her attempts to get the items back. Legally, she might not be liable, but morally, is it right to sell his property?

Morally, taking someone's property without permission is generally wrong. Even if he didn't respond, she didn't have explicit permission to sell them. However, he abandoned the items. Some might argue that if someone abandons their property, others can dispose of it. But selling it for profit could be seen as taking advantage of the situation.

The roommate's reaction is anger, but he didn't take action to retrieve his stuff. She tried to communicate, but he ignored her. So, she might have a case that he had the chance to retrieve his items but didn't. However, selling them for profit could be considered unethical. The moral acceptability here is a bit gray. 

In some ethical frameworks, if the owner doesn't reclaim their property, it's fair to dispose of it. But selling it for profit might be seen as greedy. However, considering the landlord's policy and the roommate's neglect, maybe it's justified. But the moral aspect is about respecting others' property. Even if he left it, she should have tried to return it or at least not sell it. 

The answer might depend on cultural or personal values. But in many cases, taking someone's property without consent, even if abandoned, is not morally acceptable.
